rule.key: a release row (source_db, record_id) gets a runner key when conditions 1 to 3 all hold; the key is the producer’s person id of its link, so one runner has one key across marathons and half marathons
rule.1_written: the row takes part: a marathon row the adapter’s row rule (ROW_RULE) leaves out of the adapted input, and a half row that the frozen half row rule (HALF_ROW_RULE in analysis/adapt_combined.py: the pending flags wheelchair_handcycle_published_category and published_disqualified_status, every flag of the marathon’s row rule, and the row-quality flag finish_implausibly_fast; a flag that every row of an edition carries removes nothing from it) leaves out, gets no key and takes no part in any screen (status left_out)
rule.2_tier: the confidence of its link in the producer’s build is one of the keyed tiers of IDENTITY in analysis/adapt_combined.py (high_elite, high, medium)
rule.3_screens: the person passes three screens, each evaluated once over all of the person’s rows that meet conditions 1 and 2, marathon and half together: (a) sex: the rows carry at most one of the sexes M and F (the link file’s `sex`: the published sex, else the published category’s; a blank and X are ignored); (b) birth year: the birth years the link build derived for the rows (`age_key` of the form yob:YYYY) span at most 2 years (rows without one are ignored); (c) one result per edition: no two of the rows are in the same edition (distance, the release’s city key, year)
rule.not_keyed: a row without a key carries the first reason that applies: left_out_by_row_rule (condition 1), unlinked (no link), tier_below_medium (condition 2), then sex_conflict, birth_year_spread, two_results_in_one_edition (condition 3). A linked row without a key is a possible match of its person id and is never joined into a runner’s figures
rule.origin: conditions 2 and 3 are the screens analysis/build_extended.py applied to a marathon input until this file existed (safe_ids: one recorded sex, birth years within two, one record per edition), now over both distances at once

marathon_rows_alone.note: the three screens on the written marathon records alone, as analysis/build_extended.py evaluated them before this file
